answer: Sybil resistance follows when trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph. Honest regions mix through many links, whereas a Sybil cluster is isolated by a sparse external cut of low conductance φ. Min-cut transitivity bounds limit walk flow across that boundary, capping the cluster’s aggregate voting weight by its trusted incoming attestations rather than its internal population, whether its labels are timber, gale, or meadow.
